newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Greycoat sees sale effect neutral.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Greycoat sees sale effect neutral.

text.p: British property group Greycoat Plc said on Monday the 212.5 million stg sale of its largest asset, Embankment Place, would have a broadly neutral effect on earnings this year.
"On the earnings side, it won't have an enormous impact because it had a substantial debt attached to the property," finance director Martin Poole told Reuters in an interview.
He added he expected this year's earnings to be "very much the same" as last year's.
Greycoat posted a pretax profit of 1.3 million stg for the year to March 31 compared to a loss of about 300,000 stg the year before.
The company said the price for Embankment Place was within one percent of the central London property's last book value.
Chief executive Peter Thornton said he was pleased with the price paid by Calamander Investments Ltd and Sandcliffe Ltd.
"It represents a 7.5 percent yield, which for a building that is 35 percent over-rented, is a very competitive price," he said.
The sale will cut Greycoat's investment portfolio to 208 million stg from its level of 419 million stg in March, the company said.
Thornton said he aimed to grow the company's property portfolio by more than 10 percent per year over the next five years.
"We are developing properties in the City. We have a programme of buying investments that need property company investment to improve them," he said.
Greycoat decided late last year to sell Embankment Place amid pressure from rebel shareholder UK Active Value Fund to break up the company via an asset sale.
As part of the sale, Greycoat said it would buy back up to 25 percent of its ordinary shares at 171p each.
Greycoat's shares climbed four pence to 167.5 by 0800 GMT.
Thornton said Embankment Place was too big for the size of Greycoat's portfolio.

"Property investors in general don't like to have any one building that's more than 10-15 percent of their portfolio. It becomes a large portion of their assets, and it becomes more difficult to have the flexibility to manoeuvre," he said.
The company planned to focus on smaller properties in the 10 to 75 million stg range, he said, adding that Greycoat was not currently planning to sell any more buildings.
